messages:
opsbot: Incident detected — elevated 429s for customer 'Artemis Finance' (tenant: artemis-prod) in dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu-west-2-42'. Spike started ~2026-03-15T21:05:11Z. Paging @samir-sre (on-call).

samir-sre: acked, looking. Can someone paste the pool-level QPS and per-tenant 429 rate? I'll start toggling fallback routing if this is pool-wide. paging @maria-ops for contract/override guidance.

maria-ops: got it. standing by. If it's a short burst we can do a temporary quota bump (emergency override) for artemis-prod. Need customer confirmation and impact window. @emily-cs can you confirm customer's tolerance for a short override?

emily-cs: pinged Artemis SRE (cc: @artemis-sre). Artemis: are you seeing a single job that just kicked off? can you pause it on your side while we assess? :phone:

artemis-sre: yes we just kicked a monthly reconciliation job in prod a few min ago, estimates ~5-10m heavy throughput. Can throttle it but need a short lift to avoid failing customer flows. We can throttle to ~60% if you give us a 10m bump.

rajiv-eng: quick telemetry dump below — looks like 3x baseline prefix fanout + a few hot keys. Per-tenant token rate and 429s:

```
pool: dedicated-eu-west-2-42
pool_qps: 2400 -> 7300 (5m window)
ar_temporal: artemis-prod qps: 1800 -> 5200
pool_429_rate: 0.2% -> 8.7%
ar_429_rate: 0.1% -> 12.3%
other_tenants_429: 0.05% -> 1.1%
```

rajiv-eng: root cause looks like an unthrottled batch job hitting long-sequence endpoints, KV cache thrash causing inference latency spikes and queue saturation -> downstream 429s for other tenants in same pool.

samir-sre: ok — mitigation plan A: emergency quota lift for artemis-prod + enable temporary routing to fallback model (gpt-small-quant) for background batch endpoints; mitigation plan B: isolate artemis-prod to a reserved burst lane if lift not possible. Which do we prefer? A is fastest.

maria-ops: policy note: emergency lifts require CSM signoff and a written TTL. If Artemis agrees to a 10-minute window and throttles after, Ops can authorize immediate override. We need the customer to confirm the exact start+end time.

emily-cs: Artemis confirms 10m bump starting now (they will throttle after). They also confirm they'll cap concurrency to 6 for the job. :+1:

samir-sre: executing emergency override now. Commands I ran:

```
# grant temporary rate override
redwood-admin override create --tenant artemis-prod --pool dedicated-eu-west-2-42 --rps 5200 --ttl 600
# enable fallback routing for batch endpoint
redwood-admin route update --tenant artemis-prod --endpoint "/batch/reconcile" --fallback gpt-small-quant --mode temporary
```

opsbot: Action taken: override created (id: ov-2149001111-ART). Fallback routing enabled. Notifying monitoring and customers. :white_check_mark:

samir-sre: watching metrics. initial drop in 429s within 30s but still noisy. I'll also add a soft rate limiter on non-critical prefixes to protect pool.

rajiv-eng: applied per-prefix soft caps:

```
routing.prefix_caps = {
  "/batch/": 60,    # rps per-tenant for batch prefix
  "/long/": 40
}
```

samir-sre: 2m update: pool_429_rate down to 2.1%, artemis_429 down to 1.9%. latency tails improving. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

emily-cs: Artemis SRE says their job is now at 50% concurrency and looks stable. They will fully stop after 8m. Thanks team.

artemis-sre: confirming job winding down, thanks for the quick help. We'll follow the postmortem process and share the job config.

maria-ops: override scheduled to auto-expire in 10m. Please remind me if we need to extend; otherwise this will revert. Recording the contract exception: short-term emergency lift approved by CSM (emily-cs) for 10m.

samir-sre: closing loop: pool healthy, errors back to baseline. I'll keep a watch for 15m then mark incident resolved. Great coordination. :team:

opsbot: Incident resolved — metrics stable for 15m. Closed by samir-sre. Incident notes recorded (ov-2149001111-ART).
